# App release ritual

The one runnable checklist for cutting a release of THIS app. Emitted from luxarch (`luxarch --emit release-skill`) so every repo has the identical one — do not hand-edit it above the repo's own region at its end (see the last section); re-emit to update. The *rationale* for each step lives in `luxarch --doc FLEET-RELEASE-PROCESS`; this is the runnable steps. Do them in order. A skipped step is the whole point of failure this exists to prevent (a release that tagged but never built, or shipped with a stale changelog).

> Shipping a **guard** (luxarch/luxlint/luxaudit) uses that repo's own `release` skill, not this one.

## Non-negotiables (get these wrong and you leak or break provenance)

- **Commit + tag as the fleet identity** (global git config: name `luxardolabs`, the GitHub noreply email). Just `git commit` / `git tag`; **never** `-c user.email=…`. **No AI attribution** in any message (no "Co-Authored-By", no "Generated with").
- **The git tag is `vX.Y.Z`** (leading `v`) — the git-ecosystem convention. Everything else is **bare**: the `VERSION` file, the docker `:X.Y.Z` tag, the LuxPM release version. (The `v` marks a *git tag*; it is not part of the version number.)
- **`VERSION` file at repo root is the version source of truth.** Bump it; everything derives from it.
- **Build once, deploy that artifact.** `make release` (or the repo's `dev-build-push` / `prod-deploy`) pushes the image; every node pulls it. Never deploy from local source.
- **Everything runs in Docker** — `make check`/`lint`/`test` are `docker run`; no host `.venv`.

## Steps — do every one, in order

1. **Read both writing guides in full, first; then the preconditions.** Read `<app>/change_logs/writing-guide.md` and `<app>/release_notes/writing-guide.md` before you open any previous release's files: the guides are the template for steps 5 and 6. A previous release's change log or notes is never the template. It may have drifted from the guide, and copying it carries the drift into this release. The emitted `release-docs-read-guides` hook denies writing either document until this session has read both guides. Then: a clean working tree, on the release branch. The release gate is met at step 8 — `make check` green, or every red escalated + owner-approved + recorded (a red is fixed or escalated, never released *around*).
1. **Decide the version.** Bump `VERSION` — apps are **CalVer `YYYY.0M.MICRO`** (zero-padded month; first release of a month is `.0`). Record the previous tag; you diff against it next.
1. **Gather the window (git).** `git fetch --tags`, then `git log --no-merges <last-tag>..HEAD --pretty=format:'%h %s'` and `git diff --stat <last-tag>..HEAD`. Note the issue IDs referenced, migrations added (destructive vs additive), infra/ops changes, and which surfaces changed.
1. **Reconcile the tracker (LuxPM) — audit open → closed.** `luxpm_list_issues` for open issues; for each, decide if it shipped in this window (cross-ref the step-3 commits). Close the shipped ones (`luxpm_update_issue state=done` + a `close_summary`); leave the rest open; reverse-check that every commit's issue ID resolves to a closed issue. The **closed-this-window** set is your "Issues Closed". An issue whose work carries a release action is closed here, before the tag, with its label and `Release:` line (its `release-actions/<KEY>.md` was committed with the work). Then list the **release actions** this release owes: every file under `release-actions/` in the tree (`ls release-actions/`), plus, for a final release after pre-releases, each key they consumed (the `release-actions-collected` hook names them). Each is a step or a heads-up from work this release ships: it goes into the change log in step 5, and its file is removed there.
1. **Write the technical change log — now, from the complete window** (not earlier in the cycle, and not as an afterthought *after* you ship). `<app>/change_logs/{VERSION}.md`, per `<app>/change_logs/writing-guide.md` (step 1). A changelog written early goes stale and still passes `repo.release_docs_current` (which only checks the file *exists*). Sections: Issues Closed, Features, Refactors, Schema/Migrations, Infra/Ops, Fixes, Notes. **Notes opens with `### Deploy runbook ({VERSION})`**, the one list whoever deploys follows: build it from the standing procedure (`docs/deployment/prod-release.md`), then add every one-off operator script the window ships. Find those with `git diff --name-status <last-tag>..HEAD -- '*scripts/ops/*'`, give each a row in its `scripts/ops/README.md` with `Shipped in` set to this VERSION, and make each a numbered step (dry run, then run, where it runs, the expected result, what to do on failure). List every release action from step 4 in a `### Release actions` section, `- <KEY>: <the step or heads-up>`, make each step a numbered runbook step too, and `git rm` each `release-actions/<KEY>.md` in the same commit (the emitted `release-actions-collected` hook denies the tag and `make release` while the release commit holds one, or its section leaves one out; Issues Closed does not count), Add the owner's steps from the reconciled issues (a secret, a DNS change) as runbook steps too. Every step is a make target or an exact command (FLEET-RELEASE-PROCESS §4a). `repo.ops_scripts_in_runbook` reds a script the runbook does not run.
1. **Write the user-facing release notes — now, same window.** `<app>/release_notes/{VERSION}.md`, per `<app>/release_notes/writing-guide.md` (step 1). Walk the changelog through "would a user notice this?" → NEW/IMPROVED/FIXED, written to the user, no jargon, surface badges. (Headless repo? plain-text operator labels, no badge registry — see the guide.)
1. **Cross-check the two** (FLEET-RELEASE-PROCESS §6): nothing user-visible dropped; no jargon leaked; badges are registered surfaces; both files named exactly `{VERSION}.md`; root `CHANGELOG.md` + `RELEASE_NOTES.md` pointers exist.
1. **Meet the release gate** — `make check` **green**, OR every remaining red is examined + escalated (an open tracked issue) + **owner-approved** to ship while red + recorded under `## Known reds` in `change_logs/{VERSION}.md` (name each red, its issue, why it isn't fixable locally now). Do NOT hard- stop a correctly-escalated repo: a repo tracking the guards is red-by-design between pin drops, and the fleet does not gate on red. What still blocks: an **unexamined** red, or one **deferred to green** (`[rules.deferred]`/allowlist) instead of escalated. `repo.release_docs_current` / `repo.release_docs_present` must be genuinely green (they're this release's own deliverable, never a known red). See `luxarch --doc FLEET-RELEASE-PROCESS` §0.
1. **Commit** the `VERSION` bump + both documents together: `git add -A && git commit`.
1. **Tag `vX.Y.Z`** and push it: `git tag -a v$(cat VERSION) -m v$(cat VERSION) && git push origin HEAD && git push origin v$(cat VERSION)`. To **origin**, by name: a bare `git push` follows the branch's upstream (a fork's `upstream` remote), and the Release and the image block's tag check are origin's. **Annotated (`-a`), not lightweight** — `--doc FLEET-RELEASE-PROCESS` §8 has always said so and this step said `git tag`. A lightweight tag carries no tagger or date, `git describe` ignores it by default (so the "last tag" lookup in step 3 skips it), and `git push --follow-tags` will not push it. This is the anchor the release object hangs off — do not skip it, and do not tag without the rest of this list.
1. **Run the release function — DO NOT SKIP.** `make release` (the image block: build, scan, push `:sha-<commit>` to `REGISTRY` and `:$(VERSION)` to `RELEASE_REGISTRY`, the registry prod pulls from, then the GitHub Release in step 12, which `make release-public` publishes instead when `PUBLIC_REGISTRY` is set). Before the first release from a repo whose prod pulls from another registry (prod at a host that cannot reach the local one, or GHCR), check `RELEASE_REGISTRY` is set above the block: `make -n release | grep 'docker push'` shows where each tag goes, then deploy per `luxarch --doc FLEET-BUILD-DEPLOY-STANDARD` (dev/prod), migrate the DB per `luxarch --playbook alembic`, and run the step-5 runbook's post-deploy steps. `make release` has now built and pushed this VERSION, and it refuses an already-released VERSION, so the runbook deploys the pushed `:{VERSION}` image with a target that only deploys it, never one that builds and releases again. Tagging *instead of* running this is the exact miss this checklist prevents — a tag with no shipped artifact is not a release.
1. **Publish the GitHub Release — EVERY repo, do NOT stop at the pushed image.** A git tag is NOT a Release. With the image block (v8) `make release` ends by running `make gh-release`, which creates it from `<app>/release_notes/{VERSION}.md` as the `v{VERSION}` tag holds it (gh-release block v2: commit the notes before tagging). With `PUBLIC_REGISTRY` set, `make release` leaves it to `make release-public`, which runs it after the public copy, and a standalone `make gh-release` refuses until every public `:{VERSION}` (and, with `PUBLIC_LATEST`, `:latest`) holds the released digest; confirm it with `gh release view v{VERSION} -R github.com/<owner>/<repo>`, origin's repository (`git remote get-url origin`): without `-R`, gh reads the repository it resolves (GH_REPO, `gh repo set-default`, an `upstream` remote), where another repo's Release with the same tag would confirm it. If that step failed after the push, run `make gh-release` alone (idempotent); if the public copy stopped before `:latest`, `make release-public PUBLIC_RESUME=1` finishes it and publishes the Release. A Makefile without the v8 block: `gh release create v{VERSION} -R github.com/<owner>/<repo> --verify-tag --title "{VERSION}" --notes-file <app>/release_notes/{VERSION}.md` (`--verify-tag`: without it gh creates a missing tag from the default branch's tip, a commit nobody released), and re-emit the block. This is the repo's release record — **public OR private** (a private GitHub repo has a `/releases` page too; visibility just follows the repo). Skipping it leaves `/releases` empty while the notes you wrote in step 6 sit unused (verified by `repo.github_release_wired`). Public/private only decided the *image* registry (a public repo also ran `make release-public` → GHCR); it does NOT change this step.
1. **Re-issue the LuxPM sync receipt.** `luxpm_issue_sync_receipt` for this project, written VERBATIM to `.luxpm-receipt` and committed. It expires in 14 days, so a release is where it gets refreshed — `repo.luxpm_receipt_current` reds a stale one, which is the point: a receipt proves the tracker was current *when it was issued*, and because it is signed you cannot adjust the numbers. If it reports `last_known_commit: none`, the commit ledger is not being fed — drain it with `luxpm_link_commits` (the batch tool, each commit with its `committed_at` from `git log -1 --format=%cI <sha>`, or an old sha becomes the anchor) and re-issue.
1. **Close the issue(s) this release fixes** (one with a release action was closed at step 4). `luxpm_update_issue` with `state: "done"` and a `close_summary` covering what shipped and what was measured. Anything not built is built before the release, or asked of the owner as one question when it is the owner's call (`luxarch --doc FLEET-AGENT-CONDUCT-STANDARD`, "Work what you find; never defer it"); the summary names no unbuilt work. A comment is not a close: a ticket left open after its fix is released reads as unworked, and whoever filed it is usually blocked on exactly that signal. A half-shipped fix is finished before the release, or the owner is asked whether to release without it. Close at this step, not after a deploy: the release is done when its tag, image and release record exist, and deploying it is the owner's step, never a reason to hold the issues it fixed.
1. **Mirror to LuxPM (the fleet index).** `luxpm_create_release(project=<this app's project code>, version="{VERSION}", status="released", release_date=<today>, changelog_md=<the change_logs/{VERSION}.md body>)`. This is the cross-project index + semantic-search layer, generated FROM the repo — a mirror of the GitHub Release above, not a substitute for it.

## Done when

Every step above is done: `VERSION` bumped; both `{VERSION}.md` documents written from the full window and cross-checked; every issue that shipped is closed in LuxPM (none falsely); the **release gate** met (`make check` green, or every red examined + escalated + owner-approved + listed under `## Known reds`); the `vX.Y.Z` tag pushed; the image built + pushed + **deployed**; the **GitHub Release created** (with the notes) on this repo's `/releases` — **every** repo, public or private — and **mirrored to LuxPM** (the fleet index). If the tag exists but the artifact was never built/deployed, the GitHub Release was never created (a tag is not a Release — `/releases` is empty), a red is unexamined or merely deferred, or either document is missing or stale, or a step in this repo's own region below was skipped, the release is **not** done.

## This repo's own release steps (the region at the end of this file)

The region that closes this file belongs to the repo, and no guard compares it. `repo.emitted_assets_current` reads everything above it line for line, and `luxarch --emit release-skill --update <file>` carries it across a new version. Write the repo's steps **below** its comment line, never above it.

Each step there says where it runs, by the fleet step it follows or precedes ("after step 3, before step 5: pull the product docs into `docs/product/` and commit them"), and is done as part of the release like any step above. It adds to the fleet steps and never replaces one: where the region disagrees with them, the fleet text wins. A fleet step this repo needs changed is an escalation to the guard maintainer, not a region edit.
